module_title: Requirements Documentation: BRD, PRD, and FRD
objective: Create, review, trace, govern, and defend professional Business Requirements Documents, Product Requirements Documents, and Functional Requirements Documents from beginner-level foundations through advanced integrated documentation projects.

entry_criteria.knowledge_assumption: Learners understand requirements concepts, elicitation, acceptance criteria, traceability, testing, and UAT before beginning advanced documentation work.

exit_criteria: Every listed chapter and topic has a coverage status.
Learner can select the correct document type and explain its audience, purpose, scope, and boundaries.
Learner produces a reviewed BRD, PRD, FRD, and integrated traceability matrix.
At least one guided lab and one error lab are completed or explicitly marked pseudocode.
Assignments have answer criteria and the assessment bank passes validation.
Technical and completeness audits have no unresolved critical blockers.

page_budget.target_pages: Set after chapter word budgets are approved; do not use page count as completion evidence.

risks: Confusing a PRD with the transposed abbreviation PDR or with formal design-review terminology
Duplicating requirements across documents instead of using traceable ownership boundaries
Writing solution-biased business requirements or untestable functional requirements
Treating templates as substitutes for elicitation, evidence, analysis, and stakeholder decisions
Publishing confidential, personal, security-sensitive, or proprietary information
Losing approval history, traceability, or baseline integrity during change

objective_quality.review_note: Objective names the three controlled document types and the creation, review, traceability, governance, and professional-defense competencies.
